form.4. COURSE INTENT:
Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models

labs.title: Agent Orchestration Setup
labs.exercise: Configure a local agent orchestration framework (such as LangGraph) on student development machines. Set up environment variables, configure API keys, and verify connectivity by executing a basic single-agent prompt template.

labs.title: AI-Assisted Bug Fixing
labs.exercise: Run a pre-configured coding agent on a provided Python repository to resolve simple bugs. Students must configure static analysis tools to ensure that the agent's output produces no warnings and passes all public tests.

labs.title: Multi-Agent Collaboration
labs.exercise: Implement a multi-agent system where a coder agent and a tester agent collaborate. The coder agent generates code to solve a programming task, while the tester agent executes tests and provides feedback iteratively.

labs.title: Gherkin Feature Construction
labs.exercise: Translate natural language user stories and requirements documents into Gherkin feature files for a specified use-case, ensuring complete coverage of all functional requirements.

labs.title: Executable Spec Implementation
labs.exercise: Implement step definitions in Python for the Gherkin feature files created in Week 4. Execute the specifications to validate system behavior and verify that all tests pass.

labs.title: MCP Server Setup
labs.exercise: Implement a basic server-side Model Context Protocol (MCP) connection handler. Define custom data schemas to expose local database schemas to an external agent.

labs.title: Mid-Semester Catch-up and Review
labs.exercise: Open lab session for catching up on previous labs, debugging MCP handlers, and preparing for mid-semester evaluations. No new content is introduced.

labs.title: Secure Tool Integration
labs.exercise: Integrate custom tools into an MCP server and implement secure execution of these tools using a Docker-based sandbox environment to prevent unauthorized system access.

labs.title: Agent Loop Tracing
labs.exercise: Trace the execution of an iterative coding agent loop using LangSmith. Analyze execution logs to map the agent's decision steps and identify state transitions.

labs.title: Reliability and Failure Analysis
labs.exercise: Analyze execution logs of 100 automated agent runs to identify, categorize, and document at least three distinct failure modes, providing supporting log evidence.

labs.title: Workflow Debugging
labs.exercise: Debug a failing multi-agent workflow by modifying prompt templates and tool schemas based on failure analysis, ensuring the workflow successfully completes the task.

labs.title: Multi-Component Deployment
labs.exercise: Deploy a multi-component AI-native application consisting of a frontend, an orchestrator, and multiple MCP tools using Docker Compose.

labs.title: Workflow Evaluation & Justification
labs.exercise: Conduct a structured evaluation of the deployed workflow, writing a design justification report that maps each design decision against stated system requirements.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. Target students build upon strong programming and software development fundamentals to engage in automated testing and agent-assisted coding workflows. Upon completing the course, students are able to operate coding agents using orchestration frameworks, implement agent skills and tool integrations via the Model Context Protocol, construct executable specifications from requirements documents, analyse iterative development loops with log evidence, and evaluate AI-native software development workflows for multi-component applications. The course is taught through lectures, tutorials, and practical laboratory sessions complemented by hands-on projects.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The modules progress logically from foundational agent orchestration and specification extraction to tool integration via the Model Context Protocol, iterative development tracing, and final workflow evaluation. This sequencing relies on prerequisite competencies in programming and software development established in CSE201.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment mix comprises a mid-semester examination, an end-semester examination, laboratory assignments, and a major project. This combination aligns with the practical, workflow-oriented pedagogical emphasis, directly evaluating both conceptual understanding and hands-on capability in operating coding agents and building tool integrations.
narrative.positioning_rationale: Unlike CSE701 which retrospectively examines data mining and general AI assistance, or CSE594A which focuses on algorithmic reasoning for mathematical problem-solving, this course specifically centres on software-engineering workflows, interactive coding agents, and real-time execution loops.
